concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI mandates reporting 'Fisher's z-transformed correlation deviations' for every generator evaluation. T002/T006 specify only absolute Pearson/Spearman differences and a permutation test; no task computes or reports the Fisher-z metric. This is a silent constitution drift in the task list.

T007(c) implements FR-020's faithful rule but then (e) excludes power<0.8 columns from the faithful tally, and the contract's `faithful` field bakes this in. FR-020 defines faithfulness purely as corrected p>=0.05 AND effect-size threshold; the spec's Assumptions explicitly state no power analysis is required. The task silently narrows SC-002's numerator without spec authorization.

concerns.location: tasks.md (whole document, vs constitution Reproducibility Requirements / Data Hygiene)
concerns.text: No task creates or pins `requirements.txt`/`pyproject.toml`, and no task records dataset checksums in the project state `artifact_hashes` map or updates the state file's `updated_at`. T001 only writes a local `metadata.yaml`. Constitution Principles I, III, and V have no implementing task.

FR-021 says 'randomly permuting [deferred] of rows in each column'; T007(b) says 'randomly permuted rows per column' without naming the permutation fraction or its reference. The [deferred] marker is sanctioned, but the task must still state WHAT is permuted (e.g., fraction of rows) so the value can be measured and filled in.

T004 cites the contract at `specs/001-evaluating-the-statistical-properties-of/contracts/metric_results.schema.yaml` while plan.md's project structure places it under `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/contracts/`. Two conflicting paths for the same schema will break the contract test; reconcile to one canonical path.
